title.zh: 卷三十 唐書6: 莊宗本紀四
title.en: Volume 30 Book of Later Tang 6: Zhuangzong Annals 4
title.raw: 卷三十 唐書6: 莊宗本紀四 Volume 30 Book of Later Tang 6: Zhuangzong Annals 4

sentences.zh: 同光元年冬十月辛未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, Tongguang year 1, xinwei new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei new moon of the tenth month in winter of Tongguang 1 the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇后劉氏、皇子繼岌歸鄴宮，帝送於離亭，歔欷而別。

translations.literal: That day, Empress Liu and Prince Jiji returned to the Ye palace; the Emperor saw them off at the parting pavilion and parted with sobs.
translations.idiomatic: That day Empress Liu and Prince Jiji left for Ye; Cunxu saw them off at the roadside pavilion, weeping as they parted.

sentences.zh: 詔宣徽使李紹宏、宰相豆盧革、租庸使張憲、興唐尹王正言同守鄴城。

translations.literal: He ordered Palace Secretariat commissioner Li Shaohong, chancellor Dou Luge, revenue commissioner Zhang Xian, and Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan jointly to hold Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: He left Li Shaohong of the Secretariat, Chancellor Dou Luge, revenue chief Zhang Xian, and Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan to hold Ye together.

sentences.zh: 壬申，帝御大軍自楊劉濟河。

translations.literal: On renshen the Emperor led the great army across the river from Yangliu.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Cunxu led the main force across from Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，至鄆州。

translations.literal: On guiyou he reached Yan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou he reached Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 是夜三鼓，渡汶。

translations.literal: That night at the third watch they crossed the Wen.
translations.idiomatic: That night at the third watch they forded the Wen.

sentences.zh: 時王彥章守中都。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Yanzhang was holding Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzhang was then defending Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝攻之，中都素無城守，師既雲合，梁眾自潰。

translations.literal: On jiaxu the Emperor attacked it; Zhongdu had never had proper city defenses, the armies massed like clouds, and the Liang masses collapsed on their own.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Cunxu assaulted it; Zhongdu had no real walls, his hosts closed in like clouds, and the Liang force broke apart.

sentences.zh: 是日，擒梁將王彥章及都監張漢傑、趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、康文通、王山興等將吏二百餘人，斬馘二萬，奪馬千匹。

translations.literal: That day he captured Liang general Wang Yanzhang and overseers Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Kang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and more than two hundred officers and clerks; twenty thousand heads were taken, and a thousand horses seized.
translations.idiomatic: That day he took Wang Yanzhang and overseers Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Kang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and over two hundred officers—twenty thousand heads and a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 時既獲中都之捷，帝召諸將謀其所向，或言且徇兗州，徐圖進取，唯李嗣源曰：「宜急趨汴州。

translations.literal: Now that the victory at Zhongdu was won, the Emperor summoned the generals to debate their next move; some said to sweep Yanzhou first and plan advance slowly, but only Li Siyuan said: "We should hurry on Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongdu fell Cunxu asked his generals where to strike; some urged taking Yanzhou first and advancing slowly, but Li Siyuan alone said, "March straight on Bian.

sentences.zh: 段凝方領大軍駐於河上，假如便來赴援，直路又阻決河，須自滑州濟渡，十萬之眾，舟楫焉能卒辦？

translations.literal: Duan Ning is just now leading the great army camped on the river; even if he came at once to relieve them, the direct route is blocked by the breached river and he would have to cross from Huazhou—how could a hundred thousand men ready boats overnight?
translations.idiomatic: "Duan Ning still holds the main army on the river; even if he rushed to help, the cut in the Yellow River blocks the straight road and he must cross at Huazhou—boats for a hundred thousand cannot be got in a day.

sentences.zh: 此去汴城咫尺，若晝夜兼程，信宿即至，段凝未起河堧，夷門已為我有矣。

translations.literal: From here Bian city is within a stone's throw; if we march day and night we reach it in two nights, and before Duan Ning leaves the riverbank Yimen will already be ours.
translations.idiomatic: Bian is a step away; march without rest and we are there in two nights—before Duan Ning stirs from the river, Yimen is ours.

sentences.zh: 臣請以千騎前驅，陛下禦軍徐進，鮮不克矣。

translations.literal: Your servant asks to lead a thousand horse in the van while Your Majesty brings the army slowly after—how could we fail?"
translations.idiomatic: Let me take a thousand horse ahead while Your Majesty follows with the host—we cannot miss."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu approved.

sentences.zh: 是夜，嗣源率前軍先進。

translations.literal: That night Siyuan led the vanguard forward first.
translations.idiomatic: That night Siyuan marched ahead with the van.

sentences.zh: 翌日，車駕即路。

translations.literal: Next day the imperial carriage took the road.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the court set out.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，次曹州，郡將出降。

translations.literal: On dingchou he halted at Cao prefecture; the prefect came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou he stopped at Caozhou and the prefect surrendered.

sentences.zh: 己卯遲明，前軍至汴城，嗣源令左右捉生攻封丘門，梁開封尹王瓚請以城降。

translations.literal: On jimao, as dawn was late in coming, the vanguard reached Bian city; Siyuan had his men seize prisoners and assault the Fengqiu gate, and Liang Kaifeng prefect Wang Zan asked to surrender the city.
translations.idiomatic: Near dawn on jimao the van reached Bian; Siyuan sent men to take prisoners and storm Fengqiu gate, and Liang Kaifeng prefect Wang Zan offered the city.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝與大軍繼至，王瓚迎帝自大梁門入。

translations.literal: Shortly the Emperor and the great army followed; Wang Zan welcomed the Emperor in through the Daliang gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Cunxu and the main army came up; Wang Zan received him through the Daliang gate.

sentences.zh: 梁朝文武官屬於馬前謁見，陳敘世代唐臣陷在偽廷，今日再睹中興，雖死無恨。

translations.literal: Liang civil and military officials met him before his horse and declared that for generations they had been Tang ministers trapped in the false court, and that to see restoration today they would die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: Liang officials knelt before his horse and said they had been Tang servants stuck in the usurper's court and would die content now to see restoration.

sentences.zh: 帝諭之曰：「朕二十年血戰，蓋為卿等家門無足憂矣，各復乃位。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed them: "For twenty years I have fought in blood—all so your families need not worry; each return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu told them, "Twenty years of blood I have shed so your houses may be secure—return each to his post.

sentences.zh: 」時梁末帝朱鍠已為其將皇甫麟所殺，獲其首，函之以獻。

translations.literal: " By then Liang final emperor Zhu Youzhen had already been killed by his general Huangfu Lin; his head was obtained, boxed, and presented.
translations.idiomatic: " Liang's last emperor Zhu Youzhen was already dead, killed by Huangfu Lin; his head was taken, boxed, and presented.

sentences.zh: 是日，賜樂工周匝幣帛。

translations.literal: That day he bestowed silks on the musician Zhou Za.
translations.idiomatic: That day he rewarded the actor Zhou Za with silks.

sentences.zh: 周匝者，帝之寵伶也，胡柳之役陷於梁，帝每思之，至是謁見，欣然慰接。

translations.literal: Zhou Za was the Emperor's favorite actor; at Huliu he had been captured by Liang and the Emperor had often missed him; now on meeting him he received him gladly with comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Za was Cunxu's favorite actor, lost to Liang at Huliu and long missed; now they met and he welcomed him warmly.

sentences.zh: 周匝因言梁教坊使陳俊保庇之恩，垂泣推薦，請除郡守，帝亦許之。

translations.literal: Zhou Za then spoke of the sheltering kindness of Liang Director of the Court Music Chen Jun, wept as he recommended him, and asked that he be made a prefect; the Emperor also agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Za spoke of Chen Jun of Liang's music office who had sheltered him, wept, and asked a prefecture for him; Cunxu agreed.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝御元德殿，梁百官於朝堂待罪，詔釋之。

translations.literal: On gengchen the Emperor took the Yuande Hall; Liang officials waited in the court hall to confess guilt, and an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Cunxu held Yuande Hall; Liang officials waited in court to confess guilt and were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 壬午，段凝所部馬步軍五萬解甲於封丘。

translations.literal: On renwu fifty thousand horse and foot of Duan Ning's command laid down arms at Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu fifty thousand of Duan Ning's horse and foot disarmed at Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 凝等率大將先至請死，詔各賜錦袍、御馬、金幣。

translations.literal: Ning and the rest led their great generals to come first and beg death; an edict gave each brocade robes, imperial horses, and gold and coin.
translations.idiomatic: Ning and his chief generals came first to beg death; each was given brocade robes, imperial horses, and gold.

sentences.zh: 帝幸北郊，撫勞降軍，各令還本營。

translations.literal: The Emperor went to the northern suburb, comforted the surrendered army, and ordered each to return to his original camp.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu went to the northern suburb, comforted the surrendered troops, and sent each back to his old camp.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔曰：「懲惡勸善，務振紀綱；

translations.literal: On bingxu an edict said: "To punish evil and encourage good is to uphold the statutes;
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu an edict read, "Punishing evil and encouraging good upholds the law;

sentences.zh: 激濁揚清，須明真偽。

translations.literal: to stir the muddy and lift the clear is to distinguish true from false.
translations.idiomatic: stirring the muddy and raising the clear shows truth from falsehood.

sentences.zh: 蓋前王之令典，為歷代之通規，必按舊章，以令多士。

translations.literal: These are the ordinances of former kings and the constant rule through the ages; the old regulations must be applied to command the many officers.
translations.idiomatic: Such were the laws of former kings and the rule of every age; the old code must bind the host of officers.

sentences.zh: 而有誌萌僭竊，位忝崇高，累世官而皆受唐恩，貪爵祿而但從偽命，或居台鉉，或處權衡，或列近職而預機謀，或當峻秩而掌刑憲，事分逆順，理合去留。

translations.literal: Yet there were those whose hearts harbored usurpation and theft and whose rank usurped the lofty, who for generations held office yet all received Tang grace, who coveted salary and rank yet followed only the false mandate—some sat at the imperial secretariat or held the scales of power, some held close posts and joined in plots, some held exalted rank and wielded penal law; affairs divide into rebel and loyal, and reason demands who stays and who goes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet some nursed usurpation in high place, line after line Tang servants who clung to the usurper's pay—grand councilors, power-holders, intimate plotters, chiefs of penal writs; loyalty and treason part them, and reason says who may stay.

sentences.zh: 偽宰相鄭玨等一十一人，皆本朝簪組，儒苑品流。

translations.literal: The false chancellor Zheng Jue and ten others were all pins of this court and streams of the Confucian grove.
translations.idiomatic: False chancellor Zheng Jue and ten others were court pins and Confucian men.

sentences.zh: 雖博識多聞，備明今古；

translations.literal: Though broadly learned and clear on past and present;
translations.idiomatic: Learned though they were in past and present,

sentences.zh: 而修身慎行，頗負祖先。

translations.literal: in cultivating the person and cautious conduct they greatly failed their ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: in conduct they shamed their forebears.

sentences.zh: 昧忠貞而不度安危，專利祿而全虧名節，合當大辟，無恕近親。

translations.literal: They did not weigh loyalty and constancy against safety and danger, but sought salary and rank alone and wholly ruined name and integrity—they should receive the great execution, with no indulgence for near kin.
translations.idiomatic: they weighed neither loyalty nor danger, sold honor for salary, and deserve death without kinship's mercy.

sentences.zh: 朕以纘嗣丕基，初平巨憝，方務好生之道，在行含垢之恩。

translations.literal: I, having succeeded to the great foundation and just pacified the great scourge, am about to practice the way of cherishing life and to exercise the grace of bearing filth.
translations.idiomatic: I have just taken the throne and crushed the great enemy; I mean to cherish life and bear a little filth.

sentences.zh: 湯網垂仁，既矜全族；

translations.literal: When Tang's net showed benevolence, it spared whole clans;
translations.idiomatic: When Tang's net showed mercy, whole clans lived;

sentences.zh: 舜刑投裔，兼貸一身。

translations.literal: when Shun's punishment sent men to the frontier, it still spared the person.
translations.idiomatic: when Shun exiled offenders, the man himself was spared.

sentences.zh: 爾宜自新，我全大體，其為顯列，不並庶僚。

translations.literal: You should renew yourselves; I preserve the larger frame—though you are eminent, you are not ranked with the common clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Renew yourselves; I keep the larger frame—you are eminent, not common clerks.

sentences.zh: 餘外應在周行，悉仍舊貫，凡居中外，鹹體朕懷。

translations.literal: All others who should stand in the court ranks keep their old posts; within and without, all should grasp my intent.
translations.idiomatic: All others in court rank keep their old posts; within and without, heed my intent.

sentences.zh: 」乃貶梁宰相鄭玨為萊州司戶，蕭頃為登州司戶，翰林學士劉嶽為均州司馬，任讚房州司馬，姚顗復州司馬，封翹唐州司馬，李懌懷州司馬，竇夢征沂州司馬，崇政院學士劉光素密州司戶，陸崇安州司戶，御史中丞王權隨州司戶，並員外置同正員。

translations.literal: " He then demoted Liang chancellor Zheng Jue to Lai prefecture registrar, Xiao Xiang to Deng prefecture registrar, Hanlin academician Liu Yue to Jun prefecture vice-marshal, Ren Zan to Fang prefecture vice-marshal, Yao Yi to Fu prefecture vice-marshal, Feng Qiao to Tang prefecture vice-marshal, Li Yin to Huai prefecture vice-marshal, Dou Mengzheng to Yi prefecture vice-marshal, Chongzheng Academy academician Liu Guangsu to Mi prefecture registrar, Lu Chong to An prefecture registrar, and censor-in-chief Wang Quan to Sui prefecture registrar—all as supernumerary registrars with acting full rank.
translations.idiomatic: " He demoted Zheng Jue to Lai registrar, Xiao Xiang to Deng registrar, Liu Yue to Jun vice-marshal, Ren Zan to Fang vice-marshal, Yao Yi to Fu vice-marshal, Feng Qiao to Tang vice-marshal, Li Yin to Huai vice-marshal, Dou Mengzheng to Yi vice-marshal, Liu Guangsu to Mi registrar, Lu Chong to An registrar, and Wang Quan to Sui registrar—all supernumerary with acting full rank.

sentences.zh: 是日，以梁將段凝上疏奏：「梁朝權臣趙岩等，並助成虐政，結怨於人，聖政惟新，宜誅首惡。

translations.literal: That day, because Liang general Duan Ning memorialized: "Liang power ministers Zhao Yan and others all helped complete tyrannical government and bred hatred among men; the sage rule is newly begun and the chief evils should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: That day Duan Ning memorialized, "Liang power ministers such as Zhao Yan helped tyranny and bred hatred; the new rule should kill the chief culprits.

sentences.zh: 」乃下詔曰：

translations.literal: " An edict was then issued:
translations.idiomatic: " An edict followed:

sentences.zh: 朕既殄偽庭，顯平國患。

translations.literal: I have already extinguished the false court and plainly pacified the national calamity.
translations.idiomatic: I have destroyed the false court and ended the national scourge.

sentences.zh: 好生之令，含宏雖切於予懷；

translations.literal: The order to cherish life, though broad, is urgent in my breast;
translations.idiomatic: My wish to spare life is urgent in my breast,

sentences.zh: 懲惡之規，決斷難違於眾請。

translations.literal: yet the rule to punish evil cannot lightly be set aside at the multitude's plea.
translations.idiomatic: yet the multitude's call to punish evil cannot be lightly refused.

sentences.zh: 況趙岩、趙鵠等，自朕收城數日，布惠四方，尚匿跡以潛形，罔悛心而革麵，須行赤族，以謝眾心。

translations.literal: Moreover Zhao Yan, Zhao Hu, and others, from the day I took the city for several days while grace was spread in the four quarters, still hid themselves in secret and showed no repentant heart to change their faces—their whole clans must be executed to answer the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yan, Zhao Hu, and others hid for days after the city fell though grace filled the realm—they must die with their clans to satisfy the people.

sentences.zh: 其張漢傑昨於中都與王彥章同時俘獲，此際未詳行止，偶示哀矜。

translations.literal: Zhang Hanjie was captured yesterday at Zhongdu together with Wang Yanzhang; at that time his movements were not clear and pity was shown by chance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hanjie was taken at Zhongdu with Wang Yanzhang; his fate was unclear then and he was spared by chance.

sentences.zh: 今既上將陳詞，群情激怒，往日既彰於僭濫，此時難漏於網羅，宜置國刑，以塞群論。

translations.literal: Now that the chief generals have spoken and the crowd is enraged, his past usurpation and excess are plain and he cannot slip the net this time—state punishment should be applied to stop the debate.
translations.idiomatic: Now the generals speak and the crowd rages; his past crimes are plain and he cannot slip the net—let state law answer the debate.

sentences.zh: 除妻兒骨肉外，其他疏屬仆使，並從釋放。

translations.literal: Apart from wives, children, and flesh kin, other distant kin, servants, and attendants are all released.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from wives, children, and close kin, distant kin and servants are freed.

sentences.zh: 敬翔、李振，首佐朱溫，共傾唐祚，屠害宗屬，殺戮朝臣，既寰宇以皆知，在人神而共怒。

translations.literal: Jing Xiang and Li Zhen first aided Zhu Wen in overturning the Tang, slaughtered the imperial clan, and killed court ministers—known throughout the realm, they are objects of wrath for men and spirits alike.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang and Li Zhen helped Zhu Wen destroy Tang, slaughtered the imperial clan, and killed court ministers—known to all, hated by men and gods.

sentences.zh: 敬翔雖聞自盡，未豁幽冤，宜與李振並族於市。

translations.literal: Though Jing Xiang is said to have killed himself, the hidden wrong is not cleared—he and Li Zhen should have their clans executed in the market together.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jing Xiang is said to have killed himself, the wrong is not cleared—he and Li Zhen should die with their clans in the market.

sentences.zh: 疏屬仆使，並從原宥。

translations.literal: Distant kin, servants, and attendants are all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Distant kin and servants are pardoned.

sentences.zh: 朱珪素聞狡蠹，唯務讒邪，鬥惑人情，枉害良善，將清內外，須切去除，況眾狀指陳，亦宜誅戮。

translations.literal: Zhu Gui was long known as crafty vermin who devoted himself only to slander, stirred human feelings, and wrongly harmed the good; to clear inner and outer circles he must be urgently removed, and since the multitude's petitions point to him, he too should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui was long known as a slanderer who harmed the good; to clear court and camp he must go, and the petitions demand his death.

sentences.zh: 契丹實剌阿撥，既棄其母，又背其兄。

translations.literal: The Khitan Shila Aba, having abandoned his mother, also betrayed his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan Shila Aba abandoned his mother and betrayed his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 朕比重懷來，厚加恩渥，看同骨肉，錫以姓名，兼分符竹之榮，疊被頒宣之渥。

translations.literal: I treated him with double regard when he came, heaped grace upon him, regarded him as flesh kin, gave him a surname, and moreover granted him the glory of a command tally and repeated proclamations of favor.
translations.idiomatic: When he came I favored him doubly, heaped grace on him, treated him as kin, gave him a surname, and twice granted him a command.

sentences.zh: 而乃輒辜重惠，復背明廷，罔顧欺違，竄歸偽室，既同梟獍，難貸刑章，可並妻子同戮於市。

translations.literal: Yet he then betrayed heavy favor and again turned his back on the bright court, heedless of deceit, fleeing to the false house—like owl and porcupine he cannot be spared by penal law; he and his wife and children may be executed together in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he spurned that favor, fled to the usurper's court, and like owl and porcupine cannot be spared—wife and children die with him in the market.

sentences.zh: 其朱氏近親，趙鵠正身，趙嚴家屬，仰嚴加擒捕。

translations.literal: As for Zhu kin near and far, Zhao Hu in person, and Zhao Yan's household, they are ordered strictly seized.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu kin near and far, Zhao Hu himself, and Zhao Yan's household are to be seized at once.

sentences.zh: 其餘文武職員將校，一切不問。

translations.literal: All other civil and military officers, clerks, and commanders are not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: All other civil and military officers and commanders go unasked.

sentences.zh: 是日，趙嚴、張希逸、張漢傑、張漢倫、張漢融、朱珪、敬翔、李振及契丹撒剌阿撥等，並其妻孥，皆斬於汴橋下。

translations.literal: That day Zhao Yan, Zhang Xiyi, Zhang Hanjie, Zhang Hanlun, Zhang Hanrong, Zhu Gui, Jing Xiang, Li Zhen, and the Khitan Sala Aba, with their wives and children, were all beheaded below Bian bridge.
translations.idiomatic: That day Zhao Yan, Zhang Xiyi, the Zhang Hanjie brothers, Zhu Gui, Jing Xiang, Li Zhen, and the Khitan Sala Aba and their families were beheaded below Bian bridge.

sentences.zh: 又詔除毀朱氏宗廟神主，偽梁二主並降為庶人。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered the destruction of the Zhu clan temple spirit tablets; the two false Liang rulers were both reduced to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict destroyed the Zhu temple tablets and reduced both Liang rulers to commoners.

sentences.zh: 天下官名府號及寺觀門額，曾經改易者，並復舊名。

translations.literal: Official titles, prefecture names, and temple and gate plaques throughout the realm that had been changed were all restored to the old names.
translations.idiomatic: Official titles, prefecture names, and temple plaques changed under Liang were restored.

sentences.zh: 時帝欲發梁祖之墓，斫棺燔柩，河南尹張全義上章申理，乞存聖恩，

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor wished to open Liang Founder's tomb, break the coffin, and burn the bier; Henan prefect Zhang Quanyi memorialized in appeal, begging that sage grace be preserved,
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu then meant to open the Liang Founder's tomb and burn the coffin; Henan prefect Zhang Quanyi appealed to spare imperial grace,

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：張全義上言：「朱溫雖國之深讎，然其人已死，刑無可加，屠滅其家，足以為報，乞免焚斫，以存聖恩。」）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: Zhang Quanyi said, "Though Zhu Wen was the state's deep foe, the man is dead and punishment cannot be added; destroying his house is enough for revenge—I beg that burning and hacking be spared to preserve sage grace.")〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says Quanyi argued, "Zhu Wen was our deep foe, but he is dead and cannot be punished further; his house is ruin enough—spare the burning to preserve grace.")〉

sentences.zh: 帝乃止，令剗去闕室而已。

translations.literal: The Emperor then stopped and ordered only the spirit chamber scraped away.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu stopped and had only the spirit niche cleared.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，梁百官以誅凶族，於崇元殿立班待罪，詔各復其位。

translations.literal: On dinghai Liang officials, because the evil clans had been executed, formed ranks in Chongyuan Hall to await punishment; an edict restored each to his post.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Liang officials lined up in Chongyuan Hall to await punishment after the executions; each was restored to his post.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《洛陽縉紳舊聞記》載張全義表云：「伏念臣誤棲惡木，曾飲盜泉，實有瑕疵，未蒙昭雪。

translations.literal: (The 《Records of Luoyang Gentry》 carries Zhang Quanyi's memorial: "Your servant wrongly perched on a wicked tree and once drank stolen spring water; there are indeed stains upon me that have not yet been cleared by imperial grace.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Records of Luoyang Gentry》 quotes Quanyi's memorial: "I wrongly perched on a wicked tree and drank stolen spring water; stains on me have not been cleared.

sentences.zh: 」因下詔雪之。）〉

translations.literal: " An edict then cleared him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: " An edict then exonerated him.)〉

sentences.zh: 以樞密使、檢校太保、守兵部尚書郭崇韜權行中書事。

translations.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner, acting Grand Guardian, and acting Minister of War Guo Chongtao was made acting director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao, commissioner of military affairs and acting minister of war, was made acting Secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 己丑，禦崇元殿。

translations.literal: On jichou he took Chongyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou he held Chongyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 製曰：

translations.literal: An imperial pronouncement said:
translations.idiomatic: He issued a pronouncement:

sentences.zh: 仗順討逆，少康所以誅有窮；

translations.literal: Bearing the mandate to punish the rebellious, Shaokang therefore executed Youqiong;
translations.idiomatic: Bearing the mandate to punish rebels, Shaokang slew Youqiong;

sentences.zh: 纘業承基，光武所以滅新莽。

translations.literal: succeeding to the enterprise and inheriting the foundation, Guangwu therefore destroyed Xin Mang.
translations.idiomatic: succeeding to the enterprise, Guangwu destroyed Xin Mang.

sentences.zh: 咸以中興景命，再造王猷，經綸於草昧之中，式遏於亂略之際。

translations.literal: All took the bright mandate of restoration and renewed the royal plan, ordering affairs amid the wilds and checking disorder at the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: All held restoration's bright mandate, ordering the realm amid chaos.

sentences.zh: 朕以欽承大寶，顯荷鴻休，雖繼前修，固慚涼德，誓平元惡，期復本朝，屬四海之阽危，允萬邦之推戴。

translations.literal: I respectfully received the great treasure and plainly bore the vast blessing; though I follow former cultivation, I am indeed ashamed of meager virtue, vowed to pacify the chief evil and restore this court, and when the four seas were on the brink, truly the myriad states pushed me forward.
translations.idiomatic: I took the throne and bear heaven's blessing; though I follow the ancients I am ashamed of thin virtue, vowed to crush the chief evil and restore Tang, and when the realm tottered the myriad states pushed me forward.

sentences.zh: 近者親提組練，徑掃氛襖，振已墜之皇綱，殄偷安之寇孽。

translations.literal: Lately I personally led the regiments and swept straight through the baleful mist, shook the fallen imperial net, and extinguished the bandits who stole peace.
translations.idiomatic: Lately I led the hosts myself, shook the fallen imperial net, and crushed the bandits.

sentences.zh: 國讎方雪，帝道爰開，拯編氓覆溺之艱，救率土倒懸之苦。

translations.literal: The national foe is just now avenged and the imperial way newly opened, saving the common people from drowning hardship and relieving the realm's inverted suffering.
translations.idiomatic: The foe is just avenged and the Way reopened, saving the people from drowning and the realm from hanging upside down.

sentences.zh: 粵自朱溫構逆，友貞嗣凶，篡殺二君，隳殘九廟，虺毒久傷於宇宙，狼貪肆噬於華夷。

translations.literal: From Zhu Wen's founding of rebellion and Youzhen's succession of villainy, they usurped and killed two rulers and destroyed the nine temples; poison long harmed the cosmos and wolf greed devoured China.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhu Wen's revolt and Youzhen's villainy they killed two emperors and wrecked the nine temples; poison filled the world and wolves devoured China.

sentences.zh: 剝喪元良，淩辱神主，帝裏動黍離之歎，朝廷多棟橈之危。

translations.literal: They stripped away the heir and insulted the spirit tablets; the imperial city stirred sighs of millet lost and the court held peril of rotten beams.
translations.idiomatic: They robbed the heir and insulted the ancestral tablets; the capital sighed for lost millet and the court tottered on rotten beams.

sentences.zh: 棄德崇奸，窮兵黷武，戰士疲勞於力役，蒸民耗竭其膏腴，言念於斯，軫傷彌切。

translations.literal: They cast aside virtue and exalted treachery, exhausted arms in ceaseless war; warriors were worn by corvée and the people drained their fat lands—thinking of this, my grief cuts deep.
translations.idiomatic: They cast virtue aside, exhausted the realm in war, wore soldiers with labor and drained the people—my grief cuts deep.

sentences.zh: 今則已梟逆豎，大豁群情，睹曆數之有歸，實神靈之匪昧。

translations.literal: Now the rebel chief has been beheaded and the crowd's feelings greatly opened; seeing that the calendar's number has a destination, truly the spirits are not dim.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rebel chief is beheaded and feeling opens; the calendar has found its lord and the spirits are not blind.

sentences.zh: 得不臨深表誡，馭朽為懷，將宏濟於艱難，宜特行於赦宥。

translations.literal: How could I not face the deep tablet with admonition and hold rotten wood in my breast, intending broad relief amid hardship and specially issuing pardon?
translations.idiomatic: How could I not face the tablet with admonition, hold rotten wood in mind, and issue broad pardon amid hardship?

sentences.zh: 應偽命流貶責授官等，已經量移者，並可復資，徒流人放歸鄉里。

translations.literal: All who under the false mandate were exiled, demoted, or appointed to office and have already been transferred in rank may all recover their qualifications; exiles and convicts are released to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: All exiled or demoted under the false mandate who were already transferred may recover rank; exiles and convicts go home.

sentences.zh: 京畿及諸道見禁囚徒，大辟罪降從流，已下咸赦除之。

translations.literal: Prisoners now held in the capital and on the circuits—capital crimes are reduced to exile, and all below are pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners in the capital and on the circuits—capital crimes become exile, all below are pardoned.

sentences.zh: 其鄭玨等一十一人，未在移復之限。

translations.literal: Zheng Jue and the other eleven are outside the limit of transfer and restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue and the other eleven are not included.

sentences.zh: 應扈從征討將校，及諸官員、職掌節級、馬步兵士及河北諸處屯駐守戍兵士等，皆情堅破敵，業茂平淮，副予戡定之謀，顯爾忠勤之節，並據等第，續議獎酬。

translations.literal: All officers who followed in the campaign and all clerks, post holders, horse and foot soldiers, and garrison troops in Hebei and elsewhere—all were steadfast in breaking the enemy and fruitful in pacifying the Huai, matching my plan to settle the realm and showing loyal diligence; rewards will follow by grade.
translations.idiomatic: Officers who followed the campaign, clerks, garrison troops in Hebei and elsewhere—all broke the enemy steadfastly; rewards will follow by grade.

sentences.zh: 其有歿於王事未經追贈者，各與贈官；

translations.literal: Those who died in the king's service and have not yet received posthumous honors shall each receive posthumous office;
translations.idiomatic: Those who died in service and lack posthumous rank shall receive it;

sentences.zh: 如有子孫堪任使者，並量材錄任。

translations.literal: if there are sons or grandsons fit for appointment, they shall be recorded according to talent.
translations.idiomatic: fit sons and grandsons shall be appointed by talent.

sentences.zh: 應偽庭節度、觀察、防禦、團練等使及刺史、監押、行營將校等，並頒恩詔，不議改更，仍許且稱舊銜，當俟別加新命。

translations.literal: All false-court military commissioners, observers, defense commissioners, militia commissioners, prefects, supervisors, and campaign commanders shall receive grace edicts without change of title for now; they may still use their old designations until new appointments are issued separately.
translations.idiomatic: False-court commissioners, prefects, and campaign commanders receive grace edicts without change for now and may keep old titles until new orders come.

sentences.zh: 理國之道，莫若安民；

translations.literal: The way to order a state is none better than settling the people;
translations.idiomatic: To order a state, nothing surpasses settling the people;

sentences.zh: 勸課之規，宜從薄賦。

translations.literal: the rule for encouraging farming should follow light levies.
translations.idiomatic: encouraging farming means light levies.

sentences.zh: 庶遂息肩之望，冀諧鼓腹之謠。

translations.literal: Thus may the hope of resting the shoulders be fulfilled and the song of full bellies harmonized.
translations.idiomatic: So shoulders may rest and bellies be full.

sentences.zh: 應諸道戶口，並宜罷其差役，各務營農。

translations.literal: Household registers on all circuits should cease corvée and each devote himself to farming.
translations.idiomatic: Households on all circuits shall cease corvée and farm.

sentences.zh: 所係殘欠賦稅，及諸務懸欠積年課利，及公私債負等，其汴州城內，自收復日已前，並不在征理之限；

translations.literal: Outstanding taxes and levies, accumulated annual profits of various offices, and public and private debts—within Bian city, from before the day of recovery, are all outside the limit of collection;
translations.idiomatic: Outstanding taxes, office profits, and public and private debts in Bian city before recovery are not collected;

sentences.zh: 其諸道，自壬午年十二月已前，並放。

translations.literal: on the circuits, from before the twelfth month of renwu year, all are remitted.
translations.idiomatic: on the circuits all before the twelfth month of renwu year are remitted.

sentences.zh: 北京及河北先以祆祲未平，配買征馬，如有未請卻官本錢，及買馬不迨者，可放免。

translations.literal: In the northern capital and Hebei, because omens were not yet pacified, requisition horses were bought; if there remains capital not yet repaid to the government for horses bought, or horses not delivered, they may be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the northern capital and Hebei, because omens were unsettled, horses were requisitioned; unpaid capital or undelivered horses are remitted.

sentences.zh: 應有本朝宗屬及內外文武臣僚，被朱氏無辜屠害者，並可追贈。

translations.literal: All persons of this dynasty's imperial clan and civil and military officials within and without who were slaughtered without cause by the Zhu clan may receive posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial kinsmen and every civil and military officer, inside court and out, whom the Zhu had killed without cause might be raised posthumously.

sentences.zh: 如有子孫及本身逃難於諸處漂寓者，並令所在尋訪，津置赴闕。

translations.literal: If there are descendants or the persons themselves who fled hardship and drifted to various places, each locality is ordered to search them out, provide travel support, and send them to court.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants or survivors scattered in exile were to be found wherever they were, given travel aid, and sent to court.

sentences.zh: 義夫節婦，孝子順孫，旌表門閭，量加賑給。

translations.literal: Chaste husbands and faithful wives, filial sons and obedient grandsons—honor their gates and lanes and grant relief in measured amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Chaste husbands, faithful wives, filial sons, and obedient grandsons were to have their gates honored and receive measured relief.

sentences.zh: 或鰥寡惸獨，無所告者，仰所在各議拯救。

translations.literal: Or widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary with no one to plead for them—each locality shall deliberate on rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the utterly alone with no one to speak for them were left to local rescue.

sentences.zh: 民年過八十者，免一子從征。

translations.literal: Commoners over eighty are exempt from one son's military levy.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women over eighty were freed from one son's campaign levy.

sentences.zh: 其有先投過偽庭將校官吏等，一切不問雲。

translations.literal: Those who earlier went over to the bogus court's officers and officials—all shall not be questioned, thus.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who had earlier joined the false court as officer or official was pardoned without question.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以樞密使、檢校太保、守兵部尚書、太原縣男郭崇韜為開府儀同三司、守侍中、監修國史、兼真定尹、成德軍節度使，依前樞密使、太原郡侯，仍賜鐵券。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner, acting Grand Guardian, acting Minister of War, Baron of Taiyuan Guo Chongtao was made Grand Preceptor with the honor of an opening office, acting Palace Attendant, overseer of compilation of the national history, concurrent Zhending prefect, and Chengde military commissioner; he remained Military Affairs commissioner and Marquis of Taiyuan as before, and was also granted an iron certificate.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Guo Chongtao—Military Affairs commissioner, acting Taibao, acting war minister, Baron of Taiyuan—became Grand Preceptor with opening-office honors, acting Palace Attendant, national-history overseer, Zhending prefect, and Chengde commissioner, kept Military Affairs and the Taiyuan marquisate, and won an iron certificate.

sentences.zh: 乙未，詔宰相豆盧革權判吏部上銓，御史中丞李德休權判東西銓事。

translations.literal: On yiwei, an edict made chancellor Dou Lu Ge acting chief of the upper selection board of the Ministry of Personnel, and censor-in-chief Li Detiu acting chief of the eastern and western selection boards.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Dou Lu Ge was told to run the upper Personnel board and Li Detiu the eastern and western boards.

sentences.zh: 丙申，滑州留後、檢校太保段凝可依前滑州留後，仍賜姓，名紹欽。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Huazhou acting commissioner and acting Grand Guardian Duan Ning was allowed to remain Huazhou acting commissioner as before, and was granted the imperial surname with the name Shaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Duan Ning of Huazhou kept his acting post and took the imperial surname with the name Shaocheng.

sentences.zh: 以金紫光祿大夫、檢校司空、守輝州刺史杜晏球為檢校司徒，依前輝州刺史，仍賜姓，名紹虔。

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Golden Banner and Purple Gold, acting Minister of Works, acting Huizhou prefect Du Yanqiu was made acting Minister of Education, retained as Huizhou prefect as before, and granted the surname with the name Shaoqian.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yanqiu of Huizhou—Grand Master of the Golden Banner, acting Sikong—became acting Situ, stayed at Huizhou, and took the surname with the name Shaoqian.

sentences.zh: 詔處斬隨駕兵馬都監夏彥朗於和景門外。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the execution of Xia Yanlang, supervisor of the accompanying horse and foot, outside the Hejing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had Xia Yanlang, supervisor of the escort horse and foot, beheaded outside the Hejing Gate.

sentences.zh: 時宦官怙寵，廣侵占居人第舍，郭崇韜奏其事，乃斬彥朗以徇。

translations.literal: At that time eunuchs relied on favor and broadly seized civilians' houses; Guo Chongtao memorialized the matter, and Yanlang was beheaded as an example.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs had been seizing houses at will; Chongtao reported it, and Yanlang was cut down to warn the rest.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，賜百官絹二千匹、錢二百萬，職事絹一千匹、錢百萬。

translations.literal: On dingyou, officials were granted two thousand bolts of silk and two million cash; functional officials one thousand bolts and one million cash.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou every official received two thousand bolts of silk and two million cash; functional ranks half as much.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以竭忠啟運匡國功臣、天平軍節度使、開府儀同三司、檢校太傅、兼侍中、蕃漢馬步總管副使、隴西郡侯李嗣源為依前檢校太傅、兼中書令、天平軍節度使、特進，封開國公，加食邑實封，餘如故。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Meritorious Subject Who Exhausts Loyalty and Initiates Fortune to Stabilize the Realm, Tianping military commissioner, Grand Preceptor with opening-office honors, acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Palace Attendant, deputy overall commander of Tangut and Han horse and foot, Marquis of Longxi Li Siyuan was made as before acting Grand Tutor and concurrent Director of the Secretariat, Tianping military commissioner, and Special Grandee, enfeoffed Duke Who Opens the State, with added fief and real fief, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Li Siyuan of Tianping—merit grandee, Grand Preceptor, acting Grand Tutor and chancellor, deputy Tangut and Han commander, Marquis of Longxi—kept those posts, became Duke Who Opens the State, and gained fief and real fief.

sentences.zh: 以開府儀同三司、檢校太傅、北都留守、興聖宮使、判六軍諸衛事李繼岌為檢校太尉、同平章事，充東京留守。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor with opening-office honors, acting Grand Tutor, northern capital regent, Xingsheng Palace commissioner, and overseer of the Six Armies and Imperial Guards Li Jiji was made acting Grand Commandant and co-equal chief minister, and made Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiji—Grand Preceptor, acting Grand Tutor, northern capital regent, Xingsheng commissioner, and Six Armies overseer—became acting Grand Commandant, chancellor, and Eastern Capital regent.

sentences.zh: 詔御史台，班行內有欲求外職，或要分司，各許於中書投狀奏聞。

translations.literal: An edict to the Censorate: among the court ranks, any who seek an external post or wish for a detached assignment may each submit a petition to the Secretariat for memorial and report.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate was told that any court officer wanting an outside post or detached duty might petition the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 己亥，宴勳臣於崇元殿，梁室故將鹹預焉。

translations.literal: On jihai, meritorious ministers were feasted in the Chongyuan Hall; former Liang generals all attended.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the Emperor feasted his merit ministers in the Chongyuan Hall, and former Liang commanders came too.

sentences.zh: 帝酒酣，謂李嗣源曰：「今日宴客，皆吾前日之敵，一旦同會，皆卿前鋒之力也。

translations.literal: The Emperor, drunk with wine, told Li Siyuan: "Today's guests were all my enemies of yesterday; that they meet together at once is all your vanguard's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Wine-high, he told Siyuan, "Every man at this table was my enemy yesterday; that they sit here now is your van's work.

sentences.zh: 」梁將霍彥威、戴思遠等皆伏陛叩頭，帝因賜禦衣、酒器，盡歡而罷。

translations.literal: " Liang generals Huo Yanwei, Dai Siyuan, and the rest all prostrated themselves on the steps and knocked their heads; the Emperor thereupon granted them imperial robes and wine vessels, and they drank their fill before dispersing.
translations.idiomatic: " Huo Yanwei, Dai Siyuan, and the other Liang men kowtowed on the steps; he gave them court robes and wine gear, and the feast ended in full joy.

sentences.zh: 齊州刺史孟璆上章請死，詔原之。

translations.literal: Qizhou prefect Meng Qiu submitted a memorial asking for death; an edict pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Qizhou prefect Meng Qiu asked to die; the court spared him.

sentences.zh: 璆初事帝為騎將，天祐十三年，帝與劉鄩莘縣對壘，璆領七百騎奔梁，至是來請罪。

translations.literal: Qiu had early served the Emperor as a mounted officer; in Tianyou 13, when the Emperor faced Liu Yan at Shen county, Qiu led seven hundred horse in flight to Liang; now he came to beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had once been a horse officer; in Tianyou 13, when Cunxu faced Liu Yan at Shen, he took seven hundred horse to Liang—now he came to plead guilt.

sentences.zh: 帝報之曰：「爾當吾急，引七百騎投賊，何面目相見！

translations.literal: The Emperor replied: "When I was in peril you led seven hundred horse to the enemy—what face have you to see me!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "In my straits you took seven hundred horse to the enemy—how dare you show your face!

sentences.zh: 」璆惶恐請死，帝恕之。

translations.literal: " Qiu in fear begged for death; the Emperor forgave him.
translations.idiomatic: " Qiu begged for death in terror; the Emperor let him live.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to be Bei prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to Bei prefect.

sentences.zh: 庚子，帝畋於汴水之陽。

translations.literal: On gengzi the Emperor hunted on the south bank of the Bian River.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi the Emperor hunted south of the Bian.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛丑朔，有司奏：「河南州縣見使偽印，望追毀改鑄。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on the xinchou new moon, the responsible offices memorialized: "In Henan prefectures and counties there are still bogus seals in use; we ask that they be seized, destroyed, and recast.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou new moon of the eleventh month the offices reported, "Henan still uses false seals; let them be seized, melted, and recast.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: 」The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 以光祿大夫、檢校太傅、左金吾上將軍兼領左龍武軍事、汾州刺史李存渥為滑州節度使，加特進、同平章事；

translations.literal: Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Grand Tutor, Left Golden Spear senior general and concurrent commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army, Fen prefect Li Cunwo was made Huazhou military commissioner, with added Special Grandee and co-equal chief minister rank;
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunwo of Fen—acting Grand Tutor, Left Golden Spear general and Left Dragon Martial commander—became Huazhou commissioner with Special Grandee and chancellor rank;

sentences.zh: 以雜指揮散員都部署、特進、檢校太傅、忻州刺史李紹榮為徐州節度使；

translations.literal: miscellaneous command scattered-officer overall deployer, Special Grandee, acting Grand Tutor, Xin prefect Li Shaorong was made Xuzhou military commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaorong of Xin—miscellaneous-command deployer, Special Grandee, acting Grand Tutor—became Xuzhou commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以滑州兵馬留後、檢校太保李紹欽為兗州節度使。

translations.literal: Huazhou horse-and-foot acting commissioner and acting Grand Guardian Li Shaocheng was made Yanzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shaocheng, acting Huazhou commissioner, became Yanzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，鳳翔節度使、秦王李茂貞遣使賀收復天下。

translations.literal: On renyin, Fengxiang military commissioner and Prince of Qin Li Maozhen sent envoys congratulating the recovery of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Li Maozhen of Fengxiang, Prince of Qin, sent envoys to hail the reunification of the realm.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，河中節度使、西平王朱友謙來朝。

translations.literal: On guimao, Hezhong military commissioner and Prince of Xiping Zhu Youqian came to court.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Zhu Youqian of Hezhong, Prince of Xiping, presented himself at court.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，賜友謙姓，改名繼麟，帝令皇子繼岌兄事之。

translations.literal: On yisi, Youqian was granted the imperial surname and renamed Jilin; the Emperor had the prince Li Jiji treat him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Youqian took the imperial surname as Li Jilin, and the Emperor had Li Jiji honor him as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 以捧日都指揮使、博州刺史康延孝為鄭州防禦使、檢校太保，賜姓，名繼琛。

translations.literal: Sunrise Command overall commander, Bo prefect Kang Yanxiao was made Zhengzhou defense commissioner and acting Grand Guardian, granted the surname with the name Jichen.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yanxiao of Bo—Sunrise Command commander—became Zhengzhou defense commissioner and acting Taibao, taking the surname with the name Jichen.

sentences.zh: 以宋州節度使、檢校太尉、平章事袁象先依前為宋州節度使，仍賜姓，名紹安。

translations.literal: Songzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Commandant, and co-equal chief minister Yuan Xiangxian remained Songzhou military commissioner as before, and was granted the surname with the name Shaoan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xiangxian of Song—acting Grand Commandant and chancellor—kept Songzhou and took the surname with the name Shaoan.

sentences.zh: 以許州匡國軍節度使、檢校太尉、同平章事溫韜依前許州節度使，仍賜姓，名紹衝。

translations.literal: Xuzhou Kuangguo army military commissioner, acting Grand Commandant, and co-equal chief minister Wen Tao remained Xu military commissioner as before, and was granted the surname with the name Shaochong.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tao of Xu—acting Grand Commandant and chancellor—kept Xu and took the surname with the name Shaochong.

sentences.zh: 丁未，日南至，帝不受朝賀。

translations.literal: On dingwei, the winter solstice; the Emperor did not accept court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the winter solstice, the Emperor declined the usual court rites.

sentences.zh: 戊申，中書門下上言：「以朝廷兵革雖寧，支費猶闕，應諸寺監各請置卿、少卿監、祭酒、司業各一員，博士二員，餘官並停。

translations.literal: On wushen, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "Though the court's wars are quiet, expenditures are still short; each directorate under the temples and commissions should keep one director, vice director, superintendent, and libationer or rector, two erudites, and all other posts should be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen the Secretariat reported, "Though arms are still, funds run short; each temple and commission should keep one chief, one deputy, one superintendent, one libationer or rector, and two erudites, and suspend the rest.

sentences.zh: 唯太常寺事關大禮，大理寺事關刑法，除太常博士外，許更置丞一員，其王府及東宮官、司天五官正、奉御之屬，凡關不急司存，並請未議除授。

translations.literal: Only the Court of Imperial Sacrifices touches great rites and the Court of Judicial Review touches penal law; apart from erudites of Imperial Sacrifices, one vice director may be added; as for princely establishments, Eastern Palace offices, the Bureau of Astronomy's Five Offices directors, palace attendants, and all posts not urgently needed, we ask that appointment not yet be discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Only Imperial Sacrifices and Judicial Review are vital; beyond Sacrifices erudites, one vice director each may stay; princely houses, the Eastern Palace, astronomy directors, attendants, and every non-urgent post should wait for appointment.

sentences.zh: 其諸司郎中、員外應有雙曹者，且置一員。

translations.literal: For department directors and vice directors in the various bureaus that should have paired posts, only one post is to be filled for now.
translations.idiomatic: Bureaus that normally had paired directors would keep one officer for now.

sentences.zh: 左右常侍、諫議大夫、給事中、起居郎、起居舍人、補闕、拾遺，各置一半。

translations.literal: Left and right regular attendants, remonstrance grandees, petitioners, diarists of attendance, remonstrance supplementers, and remonstrance collectors—each is to be staffed at half strength.
translations.idiomatic: Regular attendants, remonstrance grandees, petitioners, diarists, supplementers, and collectors would each be halved.

sentences.zh: 三院御史仍委御史中丞條理申奏。

translations.literal: The three bureaus of censors are still to be arranged by the censor-in-chief in memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The three censorates would still be sorted by the censor-in-chief and reported up.

sentences.zh: 其停罷朝官，仍各錄名銜，具罷任時日，留在中書，候見任官滿二十五個月，並據資品，卻與除官。

translations.literal: Suspended court officers should each have name and title recorded with the date of suspension kept in the Secretariat; when a serving officer has completed twenty-five months, according to qualification and rank, office shall be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Laid-off officers would be listed with their suspension dates at the Secretariat and restored after twenty-five months in post elsewhere, by rank and seniority.

sentences.zh: 其西班上將軍已下，仍望宣示樞密院斟酌施行。

translations.literal: As for western-rank senior generals and below, we also ask that the Bureau of Military Affairs be instructed to deliberate and put measures into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Western-rank generals and below were left to the Military Affairs office to trim and enact.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: 」The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 時議者以中興之朝，事宜恢廓，驟茲自弱，頓失物情。

translations.literal: Commentators at the time said that in a restoration court affairs ought to be broad and imposing, and that such sudden self-weakening at once lost popular feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said a restored court should look grand; slashing offices overnight only chilled hearts.

sentences.zh: 己酉，詔：應隨處官吏、務局員僚、諸軍將校等，如聞前例，各有進獻，直貢章奏，不唯褻黷於朝廷，實且傍滋於誅斂，並宜止絕，以肅化風。

translations.literal: On jiyou, an edict: wherever local officials, office clerks, and army officers and commanders, if following former practice they each made offerings, directly submitted memorials, not only profaned the court but also bred exactions on the side—all are to cease, to purify custom.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou an edict barred local officials, clerks, and commanders from the old gifts and direct memorials that profaned court and fed extortion.

sentences.zh: 又詔：左降均州司馬劉嶽，有母年逾八十，近聞身故，準故事許歸，候三年喪服闋，如未量移，即卻赴貶州。

translations.literal: Another edict: Liu Yue, demoted acting prefect of Jun, had a mother over eighty who recently died; by precedent he may return home; after the three-year mourning is complete, if he has not yet been transferred, he shall then go to his place of banishment.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict let Liu Yue of Jun—demoted after his mother's death—go home for mourning and return to banishment only if still unreassigned when mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 壬子，詔取今月二十四日幸洛京，以十二月二十三日朝獻太微宮，二十四日朝獻太廟，二十五日有事於南郊。

translations.literal: On renzi, an edict fixed the twenty-fourth of this month for the imperial progress to Luoyang; on the twenty-third of the twelfth month to offer at the Supreme Subtlety Palace, on the twenty-fourth at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and on the twenty-fifth to perform the suburban sacrifice at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the court set the twenty-fourth for Luoyang, the southern-suburb rites for the twenty-fifth of the twelfth month, with Supreme Subtlety on the twenty-third and the ancestral temple on the twenty-fourth.

sentences.zh: 癸未，中書門下奏：「應隨駕及在京有帶兼官者，並望落下，隻守本官。

translations.literal: On guiwei, the Secretariat and Chancellery memorialized: "All who on the imperial train or in the capital hold concurrent posts—we ask that these be dropped and only the primary office kept.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei the Secretariat asked that everyone on the march or in the capital shed concurrent posts and keep only the main title.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: 」The edict was approved.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，以特進、檢校太傅、開封尹、判六軍諸衛事、充功德使王瓚為宣武軍節度副使，權知軍州事。

translations.literal: On yimao, Special Grandee, acting Grand Tutor, Kaifeng prefect, overseer of the Six Armies and Imperial Guards, and commissioner of merit Wang Zan was made Xuanwu army deputy military commissioner, acting administrator of the army and prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao Wang Zan—Special Grandee, acting Grand Tutor, Kaifeng prefect, Six Armies overseer, merit commissioner—became acting Xuanwu deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，以銀青光祿大夫、尚書左丞趙光允為中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿大學士；

translations.literal: On dingsi, Silver-Green Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat Zhao Guangyun was made Secretariat Vice Minister, co-equal chief minister, and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies;
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Zhao Guangyun—Silver-Green Grand Master, Left Vice Minister—became Secretariat vice minister, chancellor, and Hall of Assembled Worthies grand academician;

sentences.zh: 以朝散大夫、禮部侍郎韋說守本官、同平章事；

translations.literal: Court Gentleman for Casual Duty, Vice Minister of Rites Wei Yue retained his office and became co-equal chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yue of Rites—Court Gentleman for Casual Duty—kept his ministry and became chancellor;

sentences.zh: 以吏部侍郎、史館修撰、判館事盧文度為兵部侍郎，充翰林學士；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel, History Institute compiler, and acting institute director Lu Wendu was made Vice Minister of War and Hanlin academician;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Wendu—Personnel vice minister and History Institute compiler—became War vice minister and Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 以右散騎常侍、充宏文館學士、判館事馮錫嘉為戶部侍郎、知制誥，充翰林學士；

translations.literal: Right Regular Attendant, Hongwen Hall academician, and acting institute director Feng Xijia was made Vice Minister of Revenue, drafter of edicts, and Hanlin academician;
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xijia—Right Regular Attendant and Hongwen academician—became Revenue vice minister, edict drafter, and Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士、守尚書膳部員外郎劉句為比部郎中、知制誥，依前充職；

translations.literal: Hanlin academician and acting Vice Minister of Provisions Liu Gou was made Vice Minister of Revenue, drafter of edicts, continuing in office as before;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gou—Hanlin academician and acting Provisions vice minister—became Revenue vice minister and edict drafter, keeping Hanlin rank;

sentences.zh: 以扈鑾書製學士、行尚書倉部員外郎趙鳳為倉部郎中、知制誥，充翰林學士；

translations.literal: imperial-train document-crafting academician and acting Vice Minister of Granaries Zhao Feng was made Vice Minister of Granaries, drafter of edicts, and Hanlin academician;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng—escort document academician and acting Granaries vice minister—became Granaries vice minister, edict drafter, and Hanlin academician;

sentences.zh: 以左拾遺於嶠守本官，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Supplements Yu Qiao retained his office and became Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qiao, Left Remonstrance Supplements, kept his post and entered the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 戊午，以中書侍郎、平章事豆盧革判租庸使，兼諸道鹽鐵、轉運等使。

translations.literal: On wuwu, Secretariat Vice Minister and co-equal chief minister Dou Lu Ge was made acting grain-transport commissioner and overseer of salt, iron, and transport for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Dou Lu Ge—Secretariat vice minister and chancellor—took the grain rolls and all-circuit salt-and-iron transport.

sentences.zh: 新羅王金樸英遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: King Geum Pung-yeong of Silla sent envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: Silla's King Geum Pung-yeong sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 己未，以洛京留守、判六軍諸衛事、守太尉、兼中書令、河南尹、魏王張全義為檢校太師、守中書令，餘如故；

translations.literal: On jiwei, Luoyang regent, overseer of the Six Armies and Imperial Guards, acting Grand Commandant, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, Henan prefect, and Prince of Wei Zhang Quanyi was made acting Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, the rest unchanged;
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Zhang Quanyi of Luoyang—Six Armies overseer, acting Grand Commandant, chancellor, Henan prefect, Prince of Wei—became acting Grand Preceptor and Secretariat director, keeping the rest;

sentences.zh: 以荊南節度使、檢校太師、守中書令、渤海王高季興依前檢校太師、守中書令，餘如故。

translations.literal: Jingnan military commissioner, acting Grand Preceptor, Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Bohai Gao Jixing remained acting Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat as before, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jixing of Jingnan—acting Grand Preceptor, chancellor, Prince of Bohai—kept those titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以工部尚書、真定尹、北都副留守、知留守事任圜為檢校吏部尚書、兼御史大夫，充成德軍節度使行軍司馬，知軍府事。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Minister of Works, Zhending prefect, northern capital deputy regent, and acting northern capital administrator Ren Yuan was made acting Minister of Personnel and concurrent Censor-in-chief, acting Chengde army campaign commander and acting administrator of the military headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Ren Yuan—Works minister, Zhending prefect, northern deputy regent—became acting Personnel minister and censor-in-chief, acting Chengde campaign commander and headquarters administrator.

sentences.zh: 安義軍節度使李繼韜入見待罪，詔釋之。

translations.literal: Anyi army military commissioner Li Jiyao came to court to await punishment; an edict released him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiyao of Anyi came to court to await judgment and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以宣化軍留後、檢校太傅戴思遠權知青州軍州事，檢校司空、左監門上將軍安崇阮並檢校舊官，卻復本任；

translations.literal: On xinyou, Xuanhua army acting commissioner and acting Grand Tutor Dai Siyuan was made acting Qing prefect; acting Sikong and Left Gate senior general An Chongruan retained their former acting ranks and returned to their original posts;
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Dai Siyuan—Xuanhua acting commissioner and acting Grand Tutor—was made acting Qing prefect; An Chongruan kept his old acting ranks and went back to his post;

sentences.zh: 以鎮國軍留後、檢校太傅霍彥威為保義軍節度留後；

translations.literal: Zhenguo army acting commissioner and acting Grand Tutor Huo Yanwei was made Baoyi army acting commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Huo Yanwei—Zhenguo acting commissioner—became Baoyi acting commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以權知威化軍留後、檢校司徒高允貞權知鎮國軍留後；

translations.literal: acting Weihua army acting commissioner and acting Minister of Education Gao Yunzhen was made acting Zhenguo army acting commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yunzhen—acting Weihua commissioner—became acting Zhenguo commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以權知河陽留後、檢校太保張繼業依前權知河陽留後；

translations.literal: acting Heyang acting commissioner and acting Grand Guardian Zhang Jiye remained acting Heyang acting commissioner as before;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiye stayed acting Heyang commissioner;

sentences.zh: 以鄜延兩鎮節度使、檢校太師、兼中書令、西平王高萬興依前鄜、延節度使，仍封北平王；

translations.literal: Yan and Yan circuits military commissioner, acting Grand Preceptor, concurrent Director of the Secretariat, and Prince of Xiping Gao Wanxing remained Yan and Yan military commissioner as before, and was also enfeoffed Prince of Northern Ping;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wanxing of Yan and Yan—acting Grand Preceptor, chancellor, Prince of Xiping—kept both circuits and was made Prince of Northern Ping;

sentences.zh: 襄州節度使、檢校太傅、平章事孔依前襄州節度使，餘如故。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou military commissioner, acting Grand Tutor, and co-equal chief minister Kong remained Xiangzhou military commissioner as before, the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Xun of Xiang—acting Grand Tutor and chancellor—kept Xiangzhou unchanged.

sentences.zh: 以永平軍節度使、行大安尹、檢校太保張筠為西都留守、行京兆尹；

translations.literal: Yongping army military commissioner, acting Da'an prefect, and acting Grand Guardian Zhang Yun was made western capital regent and acting Jingzhao prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun of Yongping—acting Da'an prefect and acting Taibao—became western capital regent and acting Jingzhao prefect;

sentences.zh: 以晉州節度使、檢校太保劉玘，邠州節度使、檢校太保韓恭，安州節度使、檢校太保朱漢賓，並檢校舊官，卻復本任。

translations.literal: Jinzhou military commissioner and acting Grand Guardian Liu Qi, Binzhou military commissioner and acting Grand Guardian Han Gong, and Anzhou military commissioner and acting Grand Guardian Zhu Hanbin all retained their former acting ranks and returned to their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi of Jin, Han Gong of Bin, and Zhu Hanbin of An kept their acting ranks and returned to their commands.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以左金吾衛大將軍史敬熔為左街使，右金吾衛大將軍李存確為右街使。

translations.literal: On renxu, Left Golden Spear Guard senior general Shi Jingrong was made Left Street commissioner, and Right Golden Spear Guard senior general Li Cunque Right Street commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Shi Jingrong of the Left Golden Spear Guard became Left Street commissioner, and Li Cunque of the Right Guard Right Street commissioner.

sentences.zh: 甲子，車駕發汴州。

translations.literal: On jiazi the imperial carriage departed Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the court left Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚午朔，車駕至西京。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on the gengwu new moon, the imperial carriage reached the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu new moon of the twelfth month the court reached Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 是日，有司自石橋具儀仗法物，迎引入於大內。

translations.literal: That day the responsible offices, from Shiqiao, prepared regalia and ritual objects and welcomed and led the Emperor into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: That day the rites office met him at Shiqiao with full regalia and escorted him into the palace.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以百官初到，放三日朝參。

translations.literal: On xinwei, because the hundred officials had just arrived, three days of court audience were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, with officials still settling in, court audience was waived for three days.

sentences.zh: 壬申，以租庸使、刑部侍郎、太清宮副使張憲為檢校吏部尚書、充北京副留守、知留守事、太原尹。

translations.literal: On renshen, grain-transport commissioner, Vice Minister of Punishments, and Grand Pure Palace deputy commissioner Zhang Xian was made acting Minister of Personnel, acting northern capital deputy regent and acting administrator, and Taiyuan prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Zhang Xian—grain commissioner, Punishments vice minister, Grand Pure deputy—became acting Personnel minister, acting northern deputy regent and administrator, and Taiyuan prefect.

sentences.zh: 詔改取來年二月一日行郊禮。

translations.literal: An edict changed the suburban rites to the first day of the second month of the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: An edict moved the suburban sacrifice to the first day of the second month next year.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，詔德勝寨、莘縣、楊劉口、通津鎮、胡柳陂皆戰陣之所，宜令逐處差人收掩戰士骸骨，量備祭奠，以慰勞魂。

translations.literal: On wuyin, an edict: Desheng Stockade, Shen county, Yangliu Ford, Tongjin Town, and Huliu Slope were all battlefields; each place should send men to gather and bury the fallen soldiers' bones, provide offerings in due measure, and comfort their spirits in toil.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the court ordered Desheng, Shen, Yangliu, Tongjin, and Huliu searched for bones, given proper burial rites to ease the dead.

sentences.zh: 詔改偽梁永平軍大安府復為西京京兆府；

translations.literal: An edict changed the bogus Liang Yongping army's Da'an prefecture back to the Western Capital Jingzhao prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored the Liang Da'an capital to the Western Capital Jingzhao;

sentences.zh: 改宋州宣武軍為歸德軍，汴州開封府復為宣武軍，滑州感化軍為鎮國軍，許州匡國軍復為忠武軍，華州宣義軍復為義成軍，陝府鎮國軍復為保義軍，耀州靜勝軍復為順義軍，潞州匡義軍復為安義軍，朗州武順軍復為武貞軍，延州為彰武軍，鄧州為威勝軍，晉州為建雄軍，安州為安遠軍。

translations.literal: changed Songzhou Xuanwu army to Guide army, Kaifeng prefecture of Bianzhou back to Xuanwu army, Huazhou Ganhua army to Zhenguo army, Xuzhou Kuangguo army back to Zhongwu army, Huazhou Xuanyi army back to Yicheng army, Shaan prefecture Zhenguo army back to Baoyi army, Yao prefecture Jingsheng army back to Shunyi army, Lu prefecture Kuangyi army back to Anyi army, Langzhou Wushun army back to Wuzhen army, Yan circuit to Zhangwu army, Deng prefecture to Weisheng army, Jin prefecture to Jianxiong army, and An prefecture to Anyuan army.
translations.idiomatic: Song became Guide, Bian Kaifeng Xuanwu again, Hua Ganhua to Zhenguo, Xu Kuangguo to Zhongwu, Hua Xuanyi to Yicheng, Shaan Zhenguo to Baoyi, Yao Jingsheng to Shunyi, Lu Kuangyi to Anyi, Lang Wushun to Wuzhen, Yan to Zhangwu, Deng to Weisheng, Jin to Jianxiong, and An to Anyuan.

sentences.zh: 淮南楊溥遣使賀登極，稱「大吳國主書上大唐皇帝」。

translations.literal: Yang Pu of Huainan sent envoys congratulating accession to the throne, styled as "the Great Wu state lord writing to the Great Tang Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu of Huainan sent envoys to hail the enthronement as "Great Wu lord to Great Tang Emperor."

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《十國春秋·吳世家》云：唐以滅梁來告，始稱詔，我國不受，唐主隨易書，用敵國禮，曰「大唐皇帝致書於吳國主」，王遣司農卿盧蘋獻金器二百兩、銀器三千兩、羅錦一千二百疋、龍腦香五斤、龍鳳絲鞵一百事於唐。

translations.literal: (The 《Spring and Autumn of the Ten States · Wu Annals》 says: When Tang reported the destruction of Liang, they first used the style of an imperial edict; our state did not accept it; the Tang ruler thereupon changed the letter and used the rites between equal states, saying "the Great Tang Emperor writes to the Wu state lord"; the king sent Court of Agriculture director Lu Ping to present to Tang two hundred liang of gold vessels, three thousand liang of silver vessels, twelve hundred bolts of silk brocade, five jin of borneol, and one hundred pairs of dragon-and-phoenix silk shoes.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Spring and Autumn of the Ten States · Wu Annals》 says when Tang announced Liang's fall it first used an edict style; Wu refused; Tang then wrote as between equals, "Great Tang Emperor to Wu lord"; the king sent Lu Ping with gold, silver, brocade, borneol, and dragon-phoenix shoes.)

sentences.zh: 又遣使張景報聘，稱「大吳國主上書大唐皇帝」，辭禮如箋表。）〉

translations.literal: He also sent envoy Zhang Jing on a return visit, styled as "the Great Wu state lord memorializing the Great Tang Emperor," with wording and rites like a memorial and table.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing followed as envoy with the style "Great Wu lord memorializing Great Tang Emperor," in memorial form.)〉

sentences.zh: 己卯，禁屠牛馬。

translations.literal: On jimao, slaughter of cattle and horses was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the court forbade killing cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，御史台上言：「請行用本朝律令格式，今訪聞唯定州有本朝法書，望下本州寫副本進納。

translations.literal: On gengchen, the Censorate memorialized: "We ask to put into use this dynasty's statutes, ordinances, and formats; on inquiry only Dingzhou has the books of law of this dynasty; we hope that prefecture may be ordered to copy a duplicate and submit it.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the Censorate asked to restore Tang law codes; only Dingzhou still held a set, and they asked for a copy.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: 」The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔貶安義軍節度使李繼韜為登州長史，尋斬於天津橋下，再謀叛故也。

translations.literal: On xinsi, an edict demoted Anyi army military commissioner Li Jiyao to long-history of Deng prefecture; soon he was beheaded below the Tianjin Bridge—for plotting rebellion again.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Li Jiyao of Anyi was demoted to Deng long-history, then beheaded at the Tianjin Bridge for plotting revolt again.

sentences.zh: 甲申，淮南楊溥、奚首領李紹威並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Yang Pu of Huainan and Xi chieftain Li Shaowei both sent envoys with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Yang Pu of Huainan and Xi leader Li Shaowei both sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以翰林學士承旨盧質權知汴州軍府事，以禮部尚書崔沂為尚書左丞、判吏部尚書銓事，以兵部侍郎崔協為吏部侍郎，以刑部侍郎、充集賢殿學士、判院事盧文紀為尚書兵部侍郎，依前充集賢殿學士、判院事。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Hanlin academician-in-chief Lu Zhi was made acting administrator of Bianzhou's military headquarters; Minister of Rites Cui Yi was made Left Vice Minister and acting chief of the Ministry of Personnel selection; Vice Minister of War Cui Xie was made Vice Minister of Personnel; Vice Minister of Punishments, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and acting institute director Lu Wenji was made Vice Minister of War, continuing as Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and acting institute director as before.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Lu Zhi—Hanlin chief—acted for Bian headquarters; Cui Yi of Rites became Left Vice Minister and acting Personnel selector; Cui Xie of War became Personnel vice minister; Lu Wenji kept Hall of Assembled Worthies and War vice minister posts.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，澤州刺史董璋上言：潞州軍變，李繼達領兵出城，自刎而死，節度副使李繼珂已安撫軍城。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Ze prefect Dong Zhang memorialized: a Luzhou army mutiny; Li Jida led troops out of the city and killed himself by the sword; deputy military commissioner Li Jike had already pacified the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Dong Zhang of Ze reported a Luzhou mutiny: Li Jida marched out and cut his own throat; deputy commissioner Li Jike had calmed the city.

sentences.zh: 己丑，有司上言：「上辛祈穀於上帝，請奉高祖神堯皇帝配；

translations.literal: On jichou, the responsible offices memorialized: "For the first si-day prayer for grain to the Supreme Lord, we ask to associate High Ancestor Shenyao Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the rites office proposed for the first si-day grain prayer to Heaven to pair High Ancestor Shenyao;

sentences.zh: 孟夏雩祀，請奉太宗文皇帝配；

translations.literal: for the midsummer rain sacrifice, we ask to associate Taizong the Cultured Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: for midsummer rain rites, Taizong the Cultured Emperor;

sentences.zh: 季秋大享於明堂，請奉太祖武皇帝配；

translations.literal: for the great autumn offering in the Bright Hall, we ask to associate Taizu the Martial Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: for the autumn Bright Hall rite, Taizu the Martial Emperor;

sentences.zh: 冬至日祀圜丘，請奉獻祖文皇帝配；

translations.literal: for the winter-solstice sacrifice at the Round Mound, we ask to associate Xianzu the Cultured Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: for winter solstice at the Round Mound, Xianzu the Cultured Emperor;

sentences.zh: 孟冬祭神州地祇，請奉懿祖昭聖皇帝配。

translations.literal: for the first winter sacrifice to the Spirit of the Land, we ask to associate Yizu the Illustrious Sage Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: for the first winter land sacrifice, Yizu the Illustrious Sage Emperor.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: 」It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: 」The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，亳州太清宮道士上言，聖祖殿前古檜萎瘁已久再生一枝，圖畫以進。

translations.literal: On xinmao, a Taoist of Taiqing Palace in Bozhou submitted word that before the hall of the Sacred Ancestor an ancient cypress, long withered, had put forth a new branch; he presented a painted image of it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao a Taoist of Bozhou's Taiqing Palace reported that before the Sacred Ancestor's hall an ancient cypress, long withered, had sprouted a new branch and submitted a painting of it.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「當聖祖舊殿生枯檜新枝，應皇家再造之期，顯大國中興之運。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Where the Sacred Ancestor's old hall bore withered cypress and new branch, it answers the royal house's term of renewed creation and shows the great state's fortune of revival.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "When the Sacred Ancestor's old hall bore new shoots on a withered cypress, it marked the royal house's renewal and the great state's revival.

sentences.zh: 同上林仆柳，祥既葉於漢宣；

translations.literal: It matches the fallen willow at Shanglin—its auspice already answered under Han Xuandi;
translations.idiomatic: Like the fallen willow at Shanglin that answered under Han Xuandi,

sentences.zh: 比南頓嘉禾，瑞更超於光武。

translations.literal: it compares to the fine grain at Nandun—a portent surpassing even Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: and like the fine grain at Nandun, a sign surpassing even Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 宜標史冊，以示寰瀛」云。

translations.literal: It should be recorded in the histories and shown to the realm" — thus.
translations.idiomatic: Let it be written in the histories and shown to the realm." Thus ended the edict.

sentences.zh: （《五代會要》云：唐高祖神堯皇帝武德二年，枯檜重華，至安祿山僭號萎瘁。

translations.literal: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 says: In Wude 2 of Tang Gaozu the Divine Yao Emperor, the withered cypress flourished anew; when An Lushan usurped the title it withered and failed.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Five Dynasties Essentials》 says: In Wude 2 of Tang Gaozu the withered cypress put out new growth; when An Lushan usurped the throne it withered again.

sentences.zh: 明皇自蜀歸京，枝葉復盛。

translations.literal: When Minghuang returned from Shu to the capital, branches and leaves flourished again.
translations.idiomatic: When Minghuang returned from Shu to the capital it flourished again.

sentences.zh: 至是再生一枝，長二尺餘。）〉

translations.literal: By this time a branch grew anew, more than two chi long.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Now a branch sprouted again, more than two chi long.)〉

sentences.zh: 壬辰，幸伊闕。

translations.literal: On renchen, the Emperor visited Yique.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the Emperor went to Yique.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以中書舍人崔居儉為刑部侍郎，充史館修撰、判館事。

translations.literal: On jisi, Palace Attendant Cui Juyi was made Vice Minister of Punishments, and charged as reviser of the History Office and chief of the institute.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Palace Attendant Cui Juyi was made Vice Minister of Punishments and charged as reviser of the History Office with direction of its affairs.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以租庸副使、光祿大夫、檢校司徒、守衛尉卿孔謙為鹽鐵轉運副使。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Assistant Commissioner for Tributary and Labor Levies, Honorary Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Acting Minister of Education, and Defender of the Guard Kong Qian was made Deputy Commissioner for Salt, Iron, and Transport.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Kong Qian, assistant commissioner for tributary and labor levies, honorary Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, acting Minister of Education, and Defender of the Guard, was made deputy commissioner for salt, iron, and transport.
